explain.say: Look at the first dot. In the 1700s, the French colony of Saint-Domingue made more sugar than almost anywhere on Earth. About half a million enslaved Africans did the work, in brutal conditions. Why was a colony like that so valuable to France?

faq.a: The French colony on the western part of the island of Hispaniola, now Haiti. In the 1780s it produced a huge share of the world's sugar and coffee, using the forced labour of about half a million enslaved people.

faq.q: How did the Haitian Revolution start?
faq.a: In August 1791, after a secret gathering remembered as Bois Caiman, enslaved people in the northern plain rose up, burning plantations and fighting for their freedom.
asks: When did the Haitian Revolution begin?

faq.a: A formerly enslaved man who became the revolution's greatest leader and general. He governed the colony by 1801, but was seized by the French in 1802 and died in a prison in France in 1803.

faq.q: Why did Napoleon send an army to Haiti?
faq.a: Napoleon wanted to restore French control and bring back slavery to make the colony profitable again. His army was defeated by Haitian fighters and by yellow fever.
asks: What did Napoleon want in Haiti?

faq.q: Why did Haiti pay France money?
faq.a: In 1825 France demanded 150 million francs, later cut to 90 million, to compensate former slave owners, in exchange for recognising Haiti. Paying it held back Haiti's economy for over a century.

facts: In 1825 France demanded an indemnity of 150 million francs from Haiti, later reduced to 90 million.
Toussaint Louverture died at Fort de Joux in France in 1803.

quiz.say: What was special about Haiti in 1804?
quiz.why: Formerly enslaved people founded a free, independent nation.

wrong.2: Haiti won its freedom from France.

quiz.say: Who led the final victory over the French army?
quiz.show: The final victory was led by…
quiz.why: Dessalines led the victory at Vertieres in 1803 and declared independence.

wrong.1: Napoleon sent the French army that was defeated.
wrong.2: Louis XVI had been executed in 1793.
